items.title: Add canonical epic manifest revision with exactly-once increment
items.description:
Give epics a canonical artifact revision so epic-scoped verification freshness has a version to compare against. Spec: 03-verification-state.md §2.2.

1. In `references/epic-manifest-schema.json`, add top-level `revision` — `{"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "description": "Canonical artifact revision for epic-scoped verification freshness."}` — and add `revision` to the schema's `required` array.
2. In `scripts/epic-manifest.py`: add `revision` to `_TOP_REQUIRED` and to the allowed top-level keys; validate it is an integer (explicitly NOT a bool) and >= 1.

4. `load_manifest(epic_dir)` presents a legacy manifest with no `revision` as logical `1` in the returned dict WITHOUT eagerly rewriting the file, so legacy validation and rendering keep working.

Funnel every increment through `_bump_and_write`: compare the proposed manifest against the on-disk manifest ignoring only `updatedAt` and the synthesized revision; if all semantic fields match, return `[]` without writing. 7. Extend `tests/test_epic_manifest.py` per 07 §4.4 rows 1-6.
8. Run `python3 scripts/build-adapters.py` and commit the regenerated adapters/.

items.description:

items.title: Route epic edit-mode from the selected member's live production state
items.description:
Fix issue #175: epic edit-mode currently routes a progressed member back to `forge-1-prd` because the exit ignores the member's actual state. Spec: 02-stage-exit-routing.md §9.

1. For `forge-0-epic --next-feature MEMBER`, resolve exactly that member under the selected epic, load its `.pipeline-state.json`, and call the existing `next_stage(state: dict) -> str | None`.
2. If state resolves, route to the returned first incomplete production stage — a member with a completed PRD resumes at tech, specs, backlog, loop, or docs, and must NOT be sent back to PRD.
3. If all production stages are complete, route to the epic dashboard rather than fabricating another member stage.
4. If state is absent, unreadable, malformed, non-object, ambiguous, escapes containment, or cannot be associated with the selected epic, emit a NAMED warning directive and fall back ONLY to `/feature-forge:forge-1-prd MEMBER`. Do not crash stage closure and do not infer later progress. This tolerant fallback is the one documented new tolerant case.
5. Creation mode is unchanged: a newly created member has no completed production stage, so it still routes to PRD.
6. An explicitly unsafe member name remains a `UsageError` exit 2 — the tolerant fallback applies to unreadable or unresolvable progress AFTER identity containment, never to path traversal.
7. Cover 07 §3.7 in `tests/test_stage_exit.py`: create an epic with one selected member at each live production position (fresh PRD, PRD complete, tech complete, specs complete, backlog complete, loop complete, all complete) and assert `next_stage` parity and the exact command. Add the negative set: missing state, corrupt JSON, non-object JSON, unreadable file, unsafe member, flat/nested collision, two-epic ambiguity, and a wrong epic back-pointer.
8. Regenerate and commit adapters/.

The warning is appended to `directives.warnings` as ENTRY 1 of that list's fixed order, using the EXACT normative template from 02 §9:
    Warning: {member}: pipeline state could not be resolved under epic {epic} ({reason}); routing to forge-1-prd. Run /feature-forge:forge {member} to inspect its state.
where {reason} is exactly one of `missing`, `unreadable`, `malformed`, or `not a member of this epic`. The template is normative — 07 §3 asserts this literal, not a paraphrase — and the trailing sentence is what satisfies REQ-OBS-02's requirement that a warning name both the affected feature and the recovery action. Do not invent additional reason strings.

items.title: Rewrite stage-exit-protocol.md as the single nine-skill scripted contract
items.description:
Make `references/stage-exit-protocol.md` the sole directive contract for all nine covered direct exits, replacing the five-stage wording and the legacy standard/warm block variants. Spec: 04-skill-integration.md §3, tech-spec §3.10.

1. Replace the existing standard/warm bespoke terminal blocks with ONE canonical stamp usable by every direct exit, retaining the portable `forge-root.sh` prelude and invoking `stage-exit` with `--feature`, `--stage`, `--specs-dir`, `--host`, `--verify-capability`, plus the stage-specific typed flags in the 04 §3.1 table.
2. Document host and capability determination (04 §3.2): `--host` describes only the adapter command surface; `--verify-capability interactive` is passed ONLY when both a question mechanism equivalent to `AskUserQuestion` AND dispatchable clean-room `forge-verifier` exist. State explicitly that `host == claude` is not a capability proxy and that capable Pi is `--host pi --verify-capability interactive`. State explicitly that clause (b) tests PERMISSION, not tool presence — "may I dispatch `forge-verifier` right now", not "is a dispatch tool listed" — because a session can carry a harness-injected standing instruction against unsolicited subagent dispatch that outranks this prose. Such a session, when it has a question mechanism, is `interactive`: the Standard Verify Gate's affirmative choice IS the user request that authorizes the dispatch. `manual` is reserved for no-question-mechanism AND no-permitted-dispatch.
3. Document the directive consumption order (04 §3.3): surface `invalidAutoVerifyKeys` and `warning` first; execute the nested chain when `runInStageVerify` — and record that this is the ONE directive asking for an unsolicited dispatch (auto-verify is authorized by config, not by a live user request), so a consent-required session presents the Standard Verify Gate first and dispatches on the affirmative choice rather than dispatching silently, skipping verification, or advancing; handle `verifyGate == standard`; for `manual-print` do not dispatch inline; print `nextSteps` byte-for-byte only when `terminalOwnedBy == "self"`.
4. Specify the Standard Verify Gate with three explicitly labeled choices, descriptions, and the recommended default (02 §5.1): Verify now (recommended); Verify now + enable auto-verify going forward; Skip for now. Advancement is allowed only after a pass or after an explicit skip is persisted.
5. State the sentinel-last rule: a direct payload contains one occurrence of the sentinel as its final line, with no summary, sign-off, warning, command result, or acceptance text after it. A nested payload has `nextSteps is None` and prints no terminal block.
6. Record that a clean-room dispatch returning `CLEAN_ROOM_UNAVAILABLE` or a non-answer means verification failed/not run: leave the debt unresolved and obtain a FRESH manual-capability payload rather than reusing one that promotes advancement.
7. Regenerate and commit adapters/.

ALSO record two contracts added in specs v4:

(a) OWNERSHIP CARRIER (04 §3.1/§5.1). A dispatching caller states branch ownership in its invocation prompt using the literal token `owner: nested` (auto-verify chains, navigator catch-up, nested re-verify) or `owner: direct`. ABSENT THE TOKEN the branch skill treats itself as `direct`, because a user-typed invocation is the only path carrying no dispatcher. Ownership is NEVER inferred from how the invocation was phrased. Getting this wrong emits a second sentinel-terminated block inside an outer stage's exit, and the §10 canon guard cannot catch it because both wordings legitimately appear in the same file.

(b) CONSENT VARIANT ON A `none` GATE (02 §5.1). When `runInStageVerify: true` and the caller may not dispatch unsolicited, the emitted `verifyGate` stays `none` — changing it to `standard` would alter directive values for existing stages 0-4 and collide with REQ-COMPAT-01. The caller reuses the SAME gate block for consent with CHOICE 2 OMITTED (auto-verify is already effective, so 'enable auto-verify going forward' is a no-op and offering a label with no trade-off violates REQ-A11Y-01). The consent form is exactly two choices: 'Verify now' (recommended) and 'Skip for now', the latter persisted as an explicit `skipped` before any advancing block. This is the ONLY case where the rendered gate and the emitted `verifyGate` value differ.

Also: the directive-order step surfaces `invalidAutoVerifyKeys` and `warnings` — a LIST rendered in 00 §4's fixed order — not a singular `warning`.
